title: fuse-flow workflow
description: A fuse-flow workflow: the ordered steps a workstream goes through, and what closes each one. Start a workstream with `fuse-flow start <slug> --workflow <name>`.

version.description: Version of the workflow file format; 1 is the only version so far. Engine effect: a file with any other value is refused, so a file written for a different format is not misread.

name.description: Human-readable name of the workflow. Engine effect: none; shown by `fuse-flow status` and the viewer.

description.description: What the workflow is for, in a sentence or two. Engine effect: none; shown by `fuse-flow list` and the viewer.

inputs.description: Documents the workflow expects from outside. Engine effect: `start --after <slug>` binds each to the earlier workstream's document with the same id, `start --input <id>=<path>` to a file, and a parent's workflow gate to its own documents. A step block shows an input that was not bound as not given.

items.description: A document the workflow expects from outside.

artifact.description: The input's id. Engine effect: steps may consume it as if an earlier step had produced it. It may not be an id a step of this workflow produces, updates or returns.

description.description: What the input is, for the reader. Engine effect: none.

required.description: Whether the workflow cannot start without it. Engine effect: `start`, and a parent creating this workflow as a child, refuse when it is not bound. Inputs are optional unless this is true.

hands_off_to.description: The workflows that may come next: one or a list, each a name or `{ workflow, when }`. Engine effect: the completion block names each with the command that starts it after this workstream; nothing starts on its own, so the owner decides.

workflow.description: The next workflow, by name or by a path relative to this workflow file.

when.description: When to start it, in words, such as once per entry of the build order. Engine effect: printed in the completion block with the start command.

workflow.description: The next workflow, by name or by a path relative to this workflow file.

when.description: When to start it, in words, such as once per entry of the build order. Engine effect: printed in the completion block with the start command.

steps.description: The steps, in the order fuse-flow runs them. The current step is the first one in the list that is neither COMPLETED nor SKIPPED, so steps run one at a time, in file order.
